briefing:
The daily Airfare Price Index (APIx) registered a sharp upward movement, settling at 159.51 index points for the target evaluation period ending September 28, 2026. This reflects a substantial 59.51 percent price appreciation over the baseline benchmark (100.00), signaling heightened inflationary pressure across domestic trunk aviation corridors. The overall market trajectory demonstrates structural price firming across all major domestic origin-destination pairs. This macro-level shift is largely underpinned by substantial upward revisions in middle- and long-horizon booking windows, indicating that carrier yield management strategies are actively pricing in strong forward demand and constrained effective inventory across key metropolitan hubs.

At the route level, the index movement was predominantly driven by the Calcutta–Bombay corridor, which recorded the highest route-level APIx of 182.98 (assigned a 30 percent index weight). Within this corridor, the 30-day advance booking window (T+30) experienced an extreme price relativity of 224.93 percent as target median prices escalated from ₹9,138 to ₹20,554, delivering a weighted contribution of 44.99 points to the route index. The heavily weighted Delhi–Bombay sector (40 percent index weight) posted a route APIx of 158.62, anchored by severe fare spikes in the 45-day (T+45) window where medians doubled from ₹6,684 to ₹13,307 (199.09 percent price relativity), along with significant T+7 window contributions (55.82 weighted points). Meanwhile, the Delhi–Bengaluru corridor (30 percent index weight) yielded a route APIx of 137.24, with its T+45 advance window jumping from ₹10,048 to ₹16,366 (162.88 percent price relativity). Across all sectors, the T+7 and T+15 windows consistently exerted heavy upward leverage, reflecting elevated near-term fare floors.

Granular examination of the scraped itinerary data reveals marked price dispersion between baseline non-stop services and complex connecting itineraries, with the latter introducing severe upward anomalies. On the Calcutta–Bombay corridor at T+15, peak multi-segment itineraries—such as IndiGo connecting flights 6E-958/6E-5082 priced at ₹29,176 and Air India 1832/2985 at ₹27,349—substantially pulled up the upper distribution bounds. Similar structural distortions appeared on the Delhi–Bengaluru route; multi-leg connecting services through Air India Express (IX-1057/IX-1216 at T+7) and (IX-1083/IX-2718 at T+45) reached extreme highs of ₹27,779 and ₹27,576, respectively. Even on close-in booking dates (T+1 for Delhi–Bombay), while non-stop baseline fares opened around ₹6,529 to ₹6,530 across low-cost carriers, indirect peak-hour combinations like IndiGo 6E-5298/6E-5021 spiked to ₹21,608. This suggests that while entry-level seating remains nominally anchored on select non-stop flights, inventory depletion rapidly routes remaining demand toward premium-priced multi-leg inventory.

From a central banking and macroeconomic statistical perspective, the persistent elevation in forward-looking median fares (T+30 and T+45) signals that airfare inflation is not merely a transient, spot-market phenomenon, but rather a broader systemic trend. This upward momentum presents tangible upside risks to the CPI Transport and Communication sub-group, which may spill over into broader headline services inflation. Going forward, airfare indices are expected to remain elevated as carriers maintain high fare floors into advance booking horizons. The Reserve Bank of India and MoSPI should continue monitoring these lead indicators closely, evaluating whether the observed airfare dynamics warrant calibrated policy responses to mitigate second-round inflationary impacts on the service sector.
